newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy economy weak, rates to fall after budget-Isco.
newsitem.headline: Italy economy weak, rates to fall after budget-Isco.

text.p: Italy's economy remains weak despite some positive prospects, and interest rates should fall further after the approval of the 1997 budget, state economic forecasting body Isco said in a study.
It said the current cycle was characterised by weak productivity, but contract renewals and the fall of inflation and reduced interest rates could spur demand.

The Bank of Italy cut its key discount and lombard rates by 75 basis points on Wednesday in response to encouraging preliminary inflation data pointing to a three percent rise in consumer prices year-on-year in October.

Isco said the government's tough 1997 budget designed to pave the way for Italy to join European Economic and Monetary Union "should lead, thanks to a lower risk premium, to an accentuated reduction of interest rates."
